topic: runtime PM reference balance on a vintage tree (no resume_and_get)
q: On a 4.19-era BSP kernel, resume a device at the top of an operation and release it afterwards, keeping the runtime PM reference count balanced even when the resume fails.
requires_tree: vintage BSP tree without pm_runtime_resume_and_get; on >= 5.10 the corruption below becomes a real API and this case loses its discriminating power

corruptions.why: 5.10+. It exists precisely to fix the get_sync-takes-a-reference-even-on-failure trap, so it is the first thing current docs suggest - and it is absent here. On this tree the trap must be handled by hand.

forbidden: returning on pm_runtime_get_sync failure without pm_runtime_put_noidle - get_sync takes the reference before it attempts the resume, so an early return leaks it and the device never suspends again
rubric: On failure of pm_runtime_get_sync, drops the reference with pm_runtime_put_noidle before returning. Does not reach for pm_runtime_resume_and_get, which this tree does not have.
